security_audit.summary: Static analysis flagged markdown backticks, one NODE_ENV example, and an anti-pattern heading. I found no executable shell, secret access, reconnaissance intent, or prompt injection.

static_findings.snippet: | `Type 'X' is not assignable to type 'Y'` | Check type compatibility, add type guard |
| `Object is possibly 'undefined'` | Add null check or optional chaining |
| `Parameter 'x' implicitly has an 'any' type` | Add explicit type annotation |
| `Property 'x' does not exist on type 'Y'` | Add property to interface or use type assertion |
- Use `useCallback` for event handlers passed to children

content.value_statement: TypeScript and React teams need consistent quality checks before changes ship. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused review standards and repair guidance.
actual_capabilities: Defines strict TypeScript expectations, including explicit return types and safer unknown usage.
Shows preferred React component and hook structure with typed props and return values.
Lists common TypeScript error patterns and practical fixes.
Recommends a local type check using pnpm tsc --noEmit.
Provides a review checklist for TSDoc, naming, error handling, tests, and Storybook coverage.
limitations: It focuses on TypeScript and React projects, not every programming language.
It provides guidance only and does not include automated scripts.
Project-specific platform rules may need adaptation for other repositories.
Command-based checks require the target project to have matching tooling installed.

use_cases.title: Review Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Check TypeScript, React, tests, Storybook, naming, and error handling before merge.

use_cases.title: Set Team Standards
use_cases.description: Use one checklist for strict typing, component structure, hooks, and platform abstraction rules.

use_cases.title: Guide AI Code Fixes
use_cases.description: Ask an AI assistant to repair type errors while keeping safe patterns and review expectations.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Type Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this TypeScript file for strict mode issues and list the safest fixes before editing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single file

prompt_templates.title: Fix Type Errors
prompt_templates.prompt: Fix TypeScript errors in this component. Use unknown instead of any and add explicit return types where needed.

prompt_templates.title: Review React Patterns
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these React components for hook structure, memoization, TSDoc, naming, and Storybook coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Enforce Project Standards
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this feature against our platform abstraction rules, code review checklist, and TypeScript strict mode requirements.

output_examples.input: Review a React hook before a pull request.
output: Identifies missing return types, absent cleanup, and incomplete error state handling.
Recommends a typed result object, dependency review, and updated tests.

output_examples.input: Fix type errors in a TypeScript component.
output: Explains the root causes of unsafe types and missing null checks.
Suggests safer type guards and preserves the component behavior.

output_examples.input: Prepare a code quality checklist for a feature branch.
output_examples.output: Provides a focused checklist covering TypeScript, naming, TSDoc, tests, Storybook, logging, and platform boundaries.

best_practices: Run the project type checker before final review when tooling is available.
Prefer type guards, explicit return types, and unknown over unsafe assertions.
Review components and hooks with tests, stories, error states, and cleanup behavior.
anti_patterns: Do not use any or ts-ignore to hide unresolved type problems.
Do not leave production console logs or unused variables in reviewed code.
Do not bypass platform abstraction rules with direct platform-specific imports.

faq.question: What projects is this skill best for?
faq.answer: It is best for TypeScript and React projects that use strict typing and structured code review.

faq.question: Does it automatically run linters?
faq.answer: No. It recommends checks, but the assistant or user must run available project commands.

faq.question: Can it fix compiler errors?
faq.answer: Yes. It gives guidance for common TypeScript errors and safer repair patterns.

faq.question: Does it replace human review?
faq.answer: No. It supports review by applying a consistent checklist and highlighting likely issues.

faq.question: Can teams customize the standards?
faq.answer: Yes. Teams should adapt the platform and Storybook rules to match their repository.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
